explorations.title: Four equally likely outcomes
explorations.instruction: Predict: will entropy be larger or smaller than for a skewed distribution? Then apply the preset, which sets n to 4 and p1, p2, p3, p4 to equal raw weights.
explorations.observe: The normalized probability readout q shows 0.25 for each active outcome, contribution readout c shows 0.5 bits per outcome, maximum entropy Hmax is 2 bits, and total entropy H is 2 bits.
explorations.why: For equally likely outcomes each q_i equals 1/n, each contribution c_i equals (1/n) log2 n, and the sum over n outcomes gives H = log2 n bits, the largest possible value for n outcomes.

explorations.title: Certainty and zero probabilities
explorations.instruction: Predict: what happens to entropy when one outcome is certain? Then apply the preset, which sets n to 3, p1 to 1, and p2, p3, p4 to 0.
explorations.observe: The normalized probability readout q shows 1 for outcome 1 and 0 for outcomes 2 and 3, every contribution c_i is 0 bits, maximum entropy Hmax is about 1.585 bits, and total entropy H is 0 bits.
explorations.why: A zero probability gives q_i = 0 and contribution c_i = 0 because an impossible outcome carries no surprise; the certain outcome also has zero contribution, so the sum H is 0 bits.
